summary:
I've been rebuilding the Japanese-learning app I use myself (Keikochō) into something that actually teaches, not just quizzes. The biggest fix this year: the app's "conversation" mode looked varied — twelve possible topics per character — but when I measured the actual answers coming back, most personas gave the same response to eleven out of twelve questions. The variety was cosmetic. The redesign keys each character's opinions off the underlying semantic category instead of the surface topic, so the answer space is actually as wide as it looks.

The image pipeline for the app taught me something I didn't expect about diffusion models: they're good at drawing a person standing somewhere, and bad — zero-for-fifteen in one test run — at drawing a person doing something communicative, like speaking or asking a question. Once I knew that, I stopped fighting the model and just wrote around the constraint (different engine for two-figure scenes, static poses for one-figure ones).

On the infrastructure side, I run a small home lab — a handful of boxes doing inference, media, and home automation — and spend a fair amount of time on the boring but important stuff: things that fail silently. One example: a GPU broker process had its restart policy set to "restart unless someone stopped it," which is exactly the setting that keeps you down after a reboot if anything stopped you first. Found it, understood why, changed the policy, moved on. I've built a handful of these deadman-switch checks over time — cheap scripts that assume a healthy system says nothing, so they go looking for evidence of life instead of waiting for evidence of failure.

I also maintain BudgetTracker, a small finance-tracking app for my own household, live at budget.phillipsben.com — nothing fancy, just receipt and shopping tracking that I actually use day to day.

highlights.oneLiner: Rebuilding Keikochō: conversation replies keyed off semantic category, not surface topic
Wrote around a diffusion-model limit: models can't draw a person speaking, only standing
Home lab deadman checks: caught a GPU broker's restart policy that couldn't survive a reboot
Household finance tracker, live, daily use for receipts and shopping
